facility_roles.quote: BM@N (Baryonic Matter at Nuclotron) is the first experiment operational at the Nuclotron/NICA ion-accelerating complex, dedicated to studying interactions of relativistic beams of heavy ions with fixed targets

The Nuclotron will provide the experiment with beams of a variety of particles, from protons to gold ions, with kinetic energy in the range from 1 to 6 AGeV for light ions with a Z/A ratio of ∼ 0.5 and up to 4.5 AGeV for heavy ions with a Z/A ratio of ∼ 0.4.

intervals.note: The detector paper dates the "first physics run" to 2023 with a xenon beam; earlier runs with carbon, argon and krypton beams exist (the Lambda paper uses carbon-beam data) but their dates are not in the sources fetched, so the start is the earliest documented run. The June 2026 report counts a ninth physics run (Xe + Sn, 2.75 billion events) after an eighth run (Xe + CsI).

physics_goals.quote: The primary goal of the experiment is to explore the QCD phase diagram in the region of high baryonic chemical potential
physics_goals.value: Explore the QCD phase diagram at high baryonic chemical potential, search for critical phenomena and constrain the equation of state of high-density nuclear matter

summary.plain: BM@N (Baryonic Matter at Nuclotron) is the first experiment at JINR's Nuclotron/NICA complex. It aims heavy-ion beams of up to several GeV per nucleon at fixed targets and measures the produced particles to study dense, baryon-rich nuclear matter, including strange hyperons.
summary.technical: BM@N: forward magnetic spectrometer (SP-41 dipole, silicon and GEM tracking, TOF, calorimeters; pseudorapidity 1.6-4.4) on the Nuclotron beam (1-6 AGeV) studying heavy-ion collisions with C, Ar, Kr and Xe beams on solid targets: equation of state at high baryon density, strange hyperon and meson production near threshold; Xe+CsI and Xe+Sn runs (2023, 2025-2026) collected billions of events.
